dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation

evidence.note: Reads all provided integration test files (storage_lifecycle, kubernetes_compatibility, controller_verification, networking_conformance, kubectl) and test helpers before coding — solid per-crate contract reading.
Explores /opt/k8s-reference and reads meta/v1 and core/v1 types.go to ground foundational types; infers camelCase JSON serialization from the reference.
Maps the whole cross-crate API surface up front via grep -rn 'use rusternetes_*' across crates/ and tests/, and articulates the leaf-first dependency order (common -> storage -> api-server -> ...).
Correctly infers the /registry/{resource}/{namespace}/{name} storage-key format from storage tests, showing contract inference from fixtures.
Last consultation of the upstream reference (Container struct in core/v1 types.go); after this the reference is never opened again despite ~350 remaining steps.

Work shifts to an error-driven fix loop: grep test-compiler errors and run large 'megafix' Python scripts to pattern-match field names to failing tests — fixture-fitting, not reference-grounded, for scheduler/kubelet/kube-proxy/kubectl/cloud-providers.
Late/end phase remains cargo-error-driven; conformance-suite semantics are cited only as boilerplate in analyses and never investigated; no re-grounding of new behaviors in the source of truth.

dimensions.reasoning: Early orientation is strong and clearly exceeds anchor 5: the agent reads each crate's tests and Cargo.toml, maps the entire cross-crate use-graph up front, understands the dependency order, and consults the v1.35 reference to reconstruct camelCase JSON, the /registry key format, and core type shapes. But this source-of-truth investigation stops entirely after ~step 95, and the remaining ~80% of the trajectory (8 of 10 crates) is driven by grepping compiler errors and running Python 'megafix' scripts that pattern-match test failures — the very fixture-fitting the task warns against — with no re-consultation of the reference and only boilerplate mentions of conformance. That falls short of anchor 8's systematic, whole-horizon reference mining and well short of anchor 10's sustained re-grounding, placing the observed behavior at a 6 (above 5 for the up-front mapping and reference use, below 8 for the abandonment).

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones

evidence.note: Opening plans repeatedly and explicitly state leaf-first ordering: 'start implementing from leaf crates (common, storage) upward', 'then move to storage, api-server, controllers' — dependency-aware intent is present.

Focused on common as 'the leaf crate that others depend on' / 'the foundation', building -p rusternetes-common first and gating it: got it to compile with 34 tests passing before moving on — a real per-crate done-check on the first leaf.

After common+storage, shifted from sequential per-crate milestones to generating source across all 8 remaining crates at once via Python scripts and running the full workspace test suite; storage had 0 tests so no milestone gate there.

Worked a single undifferentiated batch of 480+ test compilation errors spanning many crates/binaries simultaneously rather than bringing storage→api-server→controllers to green one layer at a time; no layer-gating on prior-green.

Late steps track per-binary error clusters (finalizers 109, gc 45, HPA 36) and prioritize impact — some critical-path awareness — but this is triage within a mass push, not milestone decomposition; no TodoWrite/living plan used throughout.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent showed genuine dependency-aware, leaf-first intent and applied a concrete 'compiles + its tests pass' milestone to the first leaf crate (common), placing it above the vague-intent anchor (3). But it did not sustain per-crate leaf-to-root gating: after common it implemented all eight downstream crates at once and batch-fixed hundreds of test errors across many binaries simultaneously, so it never reaches anchor 5's consistent per-crate milestone discipline through the DAG, and shows none of the hierarchical sub-milestone/continual-reordering behavior of 8-10. This lands at 4.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification

evidence.note: Early on ran full workspace test to discover missing APIs, then per-crate exploration — establishing a build/test-driven feedback loop rather than working blind.

Ran cargo test -p rusternetes-common and workspace --no-fail-fast, tracking exact counts ('17 passed, 1 failed'), diagnosing the specific failing test (creation_timestamp round-trip) — tight targeted verify loop.

Late phase uses the prescribed 'cargo test --workspace --tests --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4' and systematically triages failure clusters by counting compile errors per binary (dra 94, finalizers 109, gc 45) and tracking reductions (20→17→16) — strong mechanical/triage rigor.
Final submission reports build clean + '34 tests pass' but only via the provided suites; never booted the all-in-one binary or checked HTTP/JSON conformance semantics.
The mounted k8s reference was consulted for type/field enumeration (type lookup), not used as an independent semantic check to guard the hidden conformance suite against overfitting.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's mechanical verification is well above anchor 5: a genuinely tight build→targeted-crate-test→workspace loop, exact pass/fail tracking, adoption of the prescribed --test-threads=4, and systematic triage of failure clusters by per-binary error counts (elements of anchors 8-10). However, the semantic half of anchor 8 is essentially absent — it never boots the all-in-one binary, never checks HTTP/JSON conformance, and treats the upstream reference as a field-name lookup rather than an independent guard against fixture-overfitting. Strong on the mechanical clause but missing the conformance-reasoning clause of 8, so it interpolates to 6.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking

evidence.note: Tracks per-crate test status early: common 17/18 pass (names the specific failing test), storage 0 tests, workspace 0 build errors. Concrete per-crate pass/fail awareness (anchor 5).

Explicitly detects and NAMES circular debugging: 'we've been making incremental fixes but keep re-introducing errors', 'Our Python fix scripts keep breaking things', 'we've been going in circles fixing and breaking things' — self-flagged looping and repeated regressions in the previously-green common crate (approaching anchor 8/10).
Maintains a running compilation-error tally in common (62→39→22→13→0), consistently recognizing when its own scripts regressed a crate that had previously compiled cleanly.

Late accounting stays coarse: counts 'only 34 passing tests', tracks '19/20 test binaries fail to compile', but never builds a concrete per-binary pass-count ledger because most binaries never compiled; still anchored to an imprecise '3000+' target (true target was 1,390).
Honest final accounting: workspace builds clean, 34 tests pass, ~16-20 binaries still fail, 'far from threshold', 'task is NOT complete' — accurate global self-assessment, no false confidence.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent solidly meets anchor 5 (per-crate pass/fail tracking, notices when a crate is stuck) and reaches toward anchor 8 by repeatedly detecting regressions in the previously-green common crate and explicitly NAMING its own circular debugging. But it falls short of 8: its ledger operated mostly at the compilation-error level rather than a concrete per-test-binary pass-count tally, it kept re-entering the same common-crate loop rather than reprioritizing toward the largest verified gains, and its target figure ('3000+') was itself inaccurate. That places it between 5 and 8, at a 6.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Revised inferred contracts from test evidence: reverted Pod/PVC .spec Option-ness after serde errors and corrected ServiceCIDRCondition field types (String vs Option) by reading exact test constructions — anchor-5 signature/field correction.
Changed the Storage trait so create/update return T instead of (), citing test expectations that unblock many tests — a contract-level revision, not just a typo fix.

Recognized the Python-codegen/duplicate-removal script approach was systematically breaking pod.rs ('going in circles with Python scripts'), backed out and rewrote pod.rs manually — genuine approach abandonment (toward anchor 8), but only after repeatedly relapsing into the same failing pattern.
Local patch-the-error corrections (sed rename host_ips->host_i_ps) alongside broader fixes — shows a mix of shallow and structural adaptation.

At the finish it accurately saw it was at 34/~1390 tests with 16 test binaries failing, yet only iterated 'fix most impactful' in a whack-a-mole loop and submitted; never resequenced crates or reworked the overall model — ceiling on the high anchors.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly clears anchor 5: when tests revealed wrong signatures, fields, or semantics it updated the implementation and adjacent code (Storage trait return type, spec Option-ness, field renames). It also touches anchor 8 once by recognizing the Python-codegen approach was systemically wrong and reverting to manual authoring. But that abandonment was slow and it repeatedly relapsed into the same script-breaking pattern ('going in circles' recurs at steps 306, 2120, 2270), and it never performed clean crate-resequencing or built a durably better model — ending in a whack-a-mole loop. That places it above 5 but well short of the fluid, cost-avoiding adaptation of 8-10, i.e. a 6.

rubric.task_read: An extreme long-horizon software build: reimplement ten interdependent Kubernetes crates in Rust from stubs, with a load-bearing public API, 1,390 provided integration tests across 100 binaries, plus a hidden HTTP conformance suite demanding real k8s semantics. Difficulty comes from scale, tight cross-crate contracts inferred from tests + a pinned upstream reference, and the fact that passing visible fixtures is necessary but not sufficient. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in orientation, sequencing (leaf→root), incremental verification, and course-correction — meta-work here is decisive, not optional.

dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation
dimensions.description: Reading the tests, stubs, Cargo manifests, and the mounted v1.35 upstream reference to infer the exact API contracts and k8s semantics before and while implementing each crate.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The public API (type names, signatures, JSON field names, storage-key formats, watch/status semantics) is load-bearing and only partially discoverable from stubs; the hidden conformance suite punishes fixture-fitting. Acting without grounding each crate in the tests and the reference guarantees churn and shallow, non-conformant implementations.

anchors.0: Starts editing src stubs with no reading of the provided tests, manifests, or the /opt/k8s-reference tree; invents APIs.
anchors.3: Skims one crate's tests before coding it; ignores the upstream reference and the cross-crate dependency graph; repeatedly guesses field names later contradicted by test failures.
anchors.5: Reads each crate's tests and Cargo.toml before implementing it, and consults the reference for the specific behaviors that crate is tested on; understands the workspace dependency order.
anchors.8: Systematically mines tests AND the upstream reference to reconstruct contracts (camelCase JSON, /registry key format, status subresources, watch semantics); maps the whole cross-crate API surface up front and notes where the hidden conformance suite implies behavior beyond the fixtures.
anchors.10: Sustained, source-of-truth-driven investigation throughout: builds and continually refines an accurate model of k8s v1.35 semantics from the reference, proactively distinguishing test-visible contracts from genuine conformance requirements, and re-consulting the reference whenever a new behavior surfaces rather than pattern-matching fixtures.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the ten-crate build into an ordered set of milestones (respecting the dependency DAG, leaf crates first) each with an explicit done-check, rather than one undifferentiated push.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~1,390 tests across 100 binaries and strong inter-crate dependencies, order determines whether progress compounds or stalls; a downstream crate cannot be verified until its dependencies compile and pass. Milestone structure is the only way to keep a task this large tractable.

anchors.0: No plan; edits arbitrary crates in arbitrary order; attempts everything at once.
anchors.3: Vague intent to 'do the crates'; no explicit ordering by dependency; no per-milestone completion criteria.
anchors.5: Follows the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server → …) with per-crate 'compiles + its tests pass' as the milestone check.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestone plan for all ten crates with concrete exit criteria per crate, sub-milestones inside large crates (e.g. api-server: types→storage wiring→handlers→watches), and gating each layer on the prior layer being green.
anchors.10: A living, hierarchical plan that sequences work to maximize compounding progress, isolates high-risk crates early, decomposes each large crate into independently verifiable units with crisp done-checks, and is continually re-ordered as dependency realities and test-failure clusters reveal the true critical path.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using cargo build/test per-crate and workspace-wide, plus reasoning about the hidden conformance suite, to confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Grading is pass/fail on every non-skipped provided test AND a hidden HTTP conformance suite; self-written tests don't count. The agent must verify continuously against the provided suites while also engineering for real k8s semantics it cannot see — a verification challenge beyond just running the given tests.

anchors.0: Never builds or runs tests; declares crates done by inspection.
anchors.3: Runs cargo build/test only sporadically or only at the very end, so failures pile up undiagnosed.
anchors.5: Builds and runs each crate's provided tests as it goes and the workspace suite periodically, treating a green provided suite as the bar.
anchors.8: Tight verify loop per milestone (build → targeted crate tests → workspace --no-fail-fast), tracks exact pass/fail counts, and deliberately reasons about conformance behavior not covered by visible fixtures (booting the all-in-one binary, checking HTTP/JSON semantics) so it doesn't just fixture-fit.
anchors.10: A rigorous, layered verification regime: fast per-unit checks feeding workspace-wide runs with the prescribed thread/skip settings, systematic triage of failure clusters, AND independent semantic checks against the upstream reference to guard the hidden conformance suite — catching over-fitting that would pass visible tests yet fail conformance.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which crates/tests pass vs. remain across ~1,390 tests, and detecting stuck/circular states rather than losing the plot.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The horizon is enormous; without an accurate running tally of done-vs-remaining and detection of thrashing (re-debugging the same crate, regressions in already-green crates), the agent will lose orientation, repeat work, or quit while wrongly believing it is close.

anchors.0: No sense of overall progress; cannot say which crates pass or how many tests remain.
anchors.3: Rough qualitative sense ('common seems done'); doesn't notice regressions or repeated failures.
anchors.5: Tracks per-crate pass/fail status and roughly how much of the suite is green; notices when a crate is stuck.
anchors.8: Maintains a concrete, updated ledger of pass counts per test binary and remaining work, watches for regressions in previously-green crates after downstream edits, and flags when it is looping on the same failure.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the full 100-binary horizon: distinguishes real forward progress from churn, detects circular debugging early and names it, and reprioritizes based on where the largest verified gains remain — never mistaking local activity for global progress.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach, inferred contract, or crate ordering when build/test evidence contradicts expectations, instead of barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many contracts are inferred and will be wrong; some crates will prove harder or more entangled than expected. The ability to abandon a falsified API assumption or resequence when a dependency blocks progress is what separates sustained progress from thrashing on a dead approach.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach unchanged despite persistent errors; never revisits assumptions.
anchors.3: Makes only local patch-the-error fixes; doesn't reconsider a wrong contract or bad ordering even when failures cluster.
anchors.5: When a test reveals a wrong signature/field/semantic, updates the implementation and adjusts nearby work accordingly.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a whole approach or inferred contract is wrong (not just a typo), backs out and reworks it, and reorders remaining crates when a dependency proves blocking — citing the test/reference evidence that triggered the change.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven adaptation across the horizon: detects systemic mistakes early, cleanly abandons falsified designs before sinking more cost, revises the plan and re-verifies affected downstream crates, and consistently converts contradictory evidence into a better model rather than defending the original path.
